answer: Each agent identity must anchor one distinct domain in the juniper registry. It locks a 50-credit bond in the oasis vault and posts a key-bound DNS proof to the shale ledger; auditors re-query the record and reject duplicates. A domain counts for one key only, so the kth fake still needs its own domain at 40 credits plus the 50 bond: 90 per fake, 90,000 for 1,000 fakes, with no bulk discount. A rented-domain farm fails because a rented record carries the owner's key, not the applicant's, and a mismatch burns both bonds. An honest agent pays one set and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
